Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates a dense opacity in the right upper lung zone that appears to extend across the expected path of the minor fissure into the middle lobe region, rather than being sharply bounded by it. This "crossing" of the fissure is a radiographic sign often associated with invasive processes like pneumonia or malignancy, as opposed to non-invasive processes which typically respect anatomical boundaries.
